name: Swipe actions
description: A list row that slides sideways to show buttons underneath, as in phone mail and task apps: swipe toward the end for Done, toward the start for Snooze or Delete. Works with touch, pen and mouse, follows the reading direction, and keyboards reach the buttons with Tab.

classes.ayy-swipe: The row: clips its content and holds the trays. Vertical drags still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
classes.ayy-swipe__content: What slides: the row's own content (often with .ayy-list__item). Opaque, with --ayy-swipe-bg (default the page colour) so the trays stay hidden under it.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions: A tray of buttons under the row, after the content in the DOM. Shows over the row while it holds keyboard focus.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--start: At the inline start: revealed by swiping toward the inline end (right in English). One positive action (Done, Read).
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--end: At the inline end: revealed by swiping toward the inline start. Up to three (Pin, Snooze, Delete), the destructive one last.
classes.ayy-swipe__action: A <button> filling the tray's height: an icon over a short label, on a tint of its colour.

default.looks: The row as it is; its trays are hidden underneath until it slides.

hover.none: No hover look; swiping works with a mouse too, and Tab reaches the buttons.

pressed.none: No pressed look on the actions; they run at once.

focus.looks: Tabbing into a tray shows it over the row, and the action gets a ring inside its edge.

disabled.none: Don't offer an action that can't run; leave it out of the tray.

selected.none: Rows select through the list they're in (aria-selected on the item), not through the swipe.

error.none: If an action fails, close the tray and say so in a toast.

loading.none: Actions run at once (optimistic); undo through the toast.

open.looks: The row has slid to show the start tray (swiped toward the inline end) or the end tray.

dragging.looks: The row follows the finger with no transition.

sizes.density: Actions are at least 4.5rem wide and as tall as the row; the row keeps its own density.
sizes.width: Fills the list's width, like the row it wraps.

js: connectSwipe(row, { onOpenChange? }) → { open(side), close(), destroy() } wires the gesture on plain markup: drag past half a tray to keep it open; a tap on the row, a tap elsewhere, Esc or an action closes it. swipeActionClass({ variant? }); swipeActionVariants.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-swipe row and wires the gesture. Methods: open("start" | "end"), close().

events.ayy-open-change: { side } — "start", "end" or null when the row closes.

props.startActions: ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline end
props.endActions: ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline start
props.contentProps: HTMLAttributes — props for the sliding content (className="ayy-list__item")

props.icon: ReactNode — an Icon above the label

a11y: Swiping is a shortcut, never the only way: offer the same actions in the row's page or a Menu, since many people can't or don't swipe.
The actions are real buttons after the content in the tab order; a tray with focus shows over the row, and Esc closes an open row.
Labels stay visible under the icons, so the tint isn't the only cue.
Undo destructive actions (a Toast with Undo) rather than asking for confirmation in the middle of a gesture.
do: Use it on phone lists for the two or three things people do to rows most: Done, Snooze, Delete.
Put the positive action at the start and the destructive one last at the end, as mail apps do.
Set --ayy-swipe-bg to the surface the list sits on (a card) so the row hides its trays.
dont: Don't use it on desktop-first layouts; show the actions on hover or in a Menu there.
Don't put more than three actions in a tray.
Don't hide an action only here.

examples.title: Task rows: Done, Pin, Snooze, Delete
